arxiv-2109-06617.title: Light unflavored vector meson spectroscopy around the mass range of 2.4 ∼ 3 2.4\sim 3 GeV and possible experimental evidence
arxiv-2109-06617.creator: Li-Ming Wang 1,3, Si-Qiang Luo 2,3,4, Xiang Liu 2,3,4,5
arxiv-2109-06617.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Li-Ming Wang 1,3, Si-Qiang Luo 2,3,4, Xiang Liu 2,3,4,5. In this work, we predict the spectroscopy behavior of these light unflavored vector mesons with masses at the range of 2.4 ∼ 3 2.4\sim 3 GeV, which are still missing in the experiment. By presenting their mass spectrum and studying their two-body Okubo-Zweig-lizuka allowed decay widths, we discuss the possible experimental evidences of these discussed states combining with the present experimental data.

arxiv-2204-07119.title: Loop representation and r-Fock measures for S ​ U ​ ( N ) SU(N) gauge theories
arxiv-2204-07119.creator: Mehdi Assanioussi, Jerzy Lewandowski
arxiv-2204-07119.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mehdi Assanioussi, Jerzy Lewandowski. In this article we continue the work on translating elements of the perturbative quantum field theory defined on Minkowski spacetime into the background independent framework of Loop Quantum Gravity. We present the construction of r-Fock measures for S ​ U ​ ( N ) SU(N) gauge theories and provide a relation between these new r-Fock measures and the difeomorphism invariant measure used in loop quantum gravity.

arxiv-2205-06834.title: Multi-variant COVID-19 model with heterogeneous transmission rates using deep neural networks Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2205-06834.creator: K.D. Olumoyin, A.Q.M. Khaliq, K.M. Furati
arxiv-2205-06834.description: Abstract Mutating variants of COVID-19 have been reported across many US states since 2021. In the fight against COVID-19, it has become imperative to study the heterogeneity in the time-varying transmission rates for each variant in the presence of pharmaceutical and non-pharmaceutical mitigation measures. We develop a Susceptible-Exposed-Infected-Recovered mathematical model to highlight the differences in the transmission of the B.1.617.

arxiv-2208-09658.title: A biologically-inspired multi-modal evaluation of molecular generative machine learning
arxiv-2208-09658.creator: Elizaveta Vinogradova, Abay Artykbayev, Alisher Amanatay, Mukhamejan Karatayev, Maxim Mametkulov, Albina Li, Anuar Suleimenov, Abylay Salimzhanov, Karina Pats, Rustam Zhumagambetov, Ferdinand Molnár, Vsevolod Peshkov, Siamac Fazli
arxiv-2208-09658.description: Abstract While generative models have recently become ubiquitous in many scientific areas, less attention has been paid to their evaluation. For molecular generative models, the state-of-the-art examines their output in isolation or in relation to its input. However, their biological and functional properties, such as ligand-target interaction is not being addressed.

arxiv-2403-08731.title: Fault Localization in a Microfabricated Surface Ion Trap using Diamond Nitrogen-Vacancy Center Magnetometry
arxiv-2403-08731.creator: Pauli Kehayias, Matthew A. Delaney, Raymond A. Haltli, Susan M. Clark, Melissa C. Revelle, Andrew M. Mounce
arxiv-2403-08731.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Pauli Kehayias, Matthew A. Delaney, Raymond A. Haltli, Susan M. Clark, Melissa C. Revelle, Andrew M. Mounce. As quantum computing hardware becomes more complex with ongoing design innovations and growing capabilities, the quantum computing community needs increasingly powerful techniques for fabrication failure root-cause analysis. This is especially true for trapped-ion quantum computing.

arxiv-2408-01155.title: Efficient conversion from fermionic Gaussian states to matrix product states
arxiv-2408-01155.creator: Tong Liu, Ying-Hai Wu, Hong-Hao Tu, Tao Xiang
arxiv-2408-01155.description: Abstract Fermionic Gaussian states are eigenstates of quadratic Hamiltonians and widely used in quantum many-body problems. We propose a highly efficient algorithm that converts fermionic Gaussian states to matrix product states. It can be formulated for finite-size systems without translation invariance, but becomes particularly appealing when applied to infinite systems with translation invariance.

arxiv-2409-17140.title: AXIS: Efficient Human-Agent-Computer Interaction with API-First LLM-Based Agents
arxiv-2409-17140.creator: Junting Lu, Zhiyang Zhang, Fangkai Yang, Jue Zhang, Lu Wang, Chao Du, Qingwei Lin, Saravan Rajmohan, Dongmei Zhang, Qi Zhang
arxiv-2409-17140.description: Abstract Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled LLM-based agents to directly interact with application user interfaces (UIs), enhancing agents’ performance in complex tasks. However, these agents often suffer from high latency and low reliability due to the extensive sequential UI interactions.

arxiv-2506-16295.title: Understanding uncertainty in Bayesian cluster analysis
arxiv-2506-16295.creator: Cecilia Balocchi, Sara Wade
arxiv-2506-16295.description: Abstract The Bayesian approach to clustering is often appreciated for its ability to provide uncertainty in the partition structure. However, summarizing the posterior distribution over the clustering structure can be challenging, due the discrete, unordered nature and massive dimension of the space.

arxiv-2507-16445.title: Miniaturized and robust tunable monochromatic magneto-optical platform for pulsed magnetic fields
arxiv-2507-16445.creator: Lev Bergsma, Zhuo Yang, Bei Sun, Yasuhiro H. Matsuda, Koichi Kindo, Hiroshi Kageyama, Hiroaki Ueda, Henrik M.Ronnow, Atsuhiko Miyata
arxiv-2507-16445.description: Abstract Tunable monochromatic magneto-transmission is one of the most established magneto-optical techniques, particularly well suited for pulsed magnetic fields. It employs fixed-wavelength monochromatic light as the probe, while the magnetic field is swept to bring the sample into resonance with the photon energy.

arxiv-2511-00591.description: Abstract The China Space Station Telescope (CSST) will conduct a deep and wide imaging survey in the N ​ U ​ V NUV -, u u -, g g -, r r -, i i -, z z -, and y y -bands. In this work, using theoretical data synthesized from the BOSZ spectra of Bohlin et al.

arxiv-2511-03103.title: Adaptive Detection of Software Aging under Workload Shift
arxiv-2511-03103.creator: Rafael José Moura 1, Maria Gizele Nascimento 1, Fumio Machida 2, Ermeson Andrade 1
arxiv-2511-03103.description: Abstract Software aging is a phenomenon that affects long-running systems, leading to progressive performance degradation and increasing the risk of failures. To mitigate this problem, this work proposes an adaptive approach based on machine learning for software aging detection in environments subject to dynamic workload conditions.

arxiv-2512-11932.title: Entanglement Evolution of Noisy Quantum Systems: Master Equation-TFD Solutions
arxiv-2512-11932.creator: Urjjarani Patel, KVS Shiv Chaitanya
arxiv-2512-11932.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Urjjarani Patel, KVS Shiv Chaitanya. In this paper, Thermofield Dynamics (TFD) is applied to map a quantum optics nonlinear master equation into a Schrödinger-like equation for any arbitrary initial condition. This formalism provides a more efficient way for solving open quantum system problems.

pmc-11649736.title: Detection and Prevalence of Coronaviruses in European Bats: A Systematic Review
pmc-11649736.creator: Mahima Hemnani, Priscilla Gomes da Silva, Gertrude Thompson, Patrícia Poeta, Hugo Rebelo, João R. Mesquita
pmc-11649736.description: Bats are known hosts for a wide range of coronaviruses (CoVs), including those that cause severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS-CoV-1) and Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS-CoV). With the emergence of the COVID-19 pandemic caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, it has become increasingly important to understand the diversity and prevalence of CoVs in bat populations.

pmc-11692725.title: ASSESSING MOBILITY AND FALL RISKS IN TAIWAN’S OLDER ADULT POPULATION: A LONGITUDINAL STUDY
pmc-11692725.creator: Fang-Lin Kuo, Zih-Yong Liao
pmc-11692725.description: Mobility difficulties impact older adults’ health significantly, leading to adverse outcomes and loss of independence. In Taiwan, 21% of community-dwelling older adults report falls, and over half have a fear of falling, highlighting the importance of identifying individuals at risk. This study aimed to explore mobility changes and repeated falls in Taiwan’s rural areas, where the older population exceeds 24%.

pmc-12606918.title: Sexual and reproductive health interventions for mobile adolescents and young people in sub-Saharan Africa: a scoping review
pmc-12606918.creator: Langelihle Mlotshwa, Simóne Plüg, Melvin Simuyaba, Natsayi Chimbindi, Darshini Govindasamy, Musonda Simwinga, Tolib Mirzoev, Janet Seeley, Nurture4Youth project team
pmc-12606918.description: BackgroundMobility among adolescents and young people (AYP) is a key factor influencing their access to sexual and reproductive health rights (SRHR) services. Young migrants are more likely to experience gender-based violence and their access to SRHR services and education is often limited in their new communities.

pmc-12734963.title: The Influence and Compensation of Process on Measurement Accuracy in Digital Grating Focusing and Leveling Sensors
pmc-12734963.creator: Shiguang Li, Xianjie Li, Guocai He
pmc-12734963.description: The digital grating focusing and leveling sensor is a kind of wafer height sensor for focus control in a lithography tool by measuring the displacement of an optical grating image reflected from the wafer surface. The process pattern on the wafer surface can significantly affect the measurement accuracy of the sensor.

pmc-12744267.title: Microscale pressure measurements and optical coherence tomography reveal time-dependent biomechanical stages of ovulation in mice
pmc-12744267.creator: Emily J. Zaniker-Gomez, Zihang Yan, Jing Yang, Darryl L. Russell, Hao Zhang, Sean X. Sun, Francesca E. Duncan
pmc-12744267.description: SummaryDuring ovulation, antral follicles undergo coordinated remodeling that results in egg release and corpora lutea formation, which are key processes for fertility and endocrine function. Using an ex vivo murine ovulation model integrated with time-lapse imaging, microscale pressure sensing, and optical coherence tomography (OCT), we characterized and quantified the sequence of mechanical events driving follicle rupture.

pmc-13651021.title: Youth perspectives on how social influences impacted nicotine vaping cessation: A qualitative thematic analysis
pmc-13651021.creator: Laura Struik, M Taylor, D Rodberg, R Nawara, K Fonteyne, T Afshar, Y Yang
pmc-13651021.description: BackgroundIt is well known that social influences play a major role in nicotine vaping uptake among youth. However, little is known about how these influences play a role in nicotine vaping cessation. This research article examines the complex social influences on youth nicotine vaping cessation.
